transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for taking my call. Yes, I do have some questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So with gardening, you should avoid any exercise for the first week after your surgery. After that first week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening, so you'd be fine to start doing a bit of gardening from week two onwards.

Just make sure you're being gentle with yourself and not doing anything too strenuous.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know, thank you! Next, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it after surgery, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be fine to keep using it as you were before. If you're running low and need more, your GP should be able to provide some.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that's reassuring. I do have another question: I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
It's quite common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, it would be best to contact your care team.

Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's quite common for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
No problem! It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. 

However, I don't have the details of exactly when your surgery was, so I'm not sure how far along you are in your recovery. If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

But before we move on — I want to finish answering your earlier question about the light sensitivity. The important thing to know is that significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, is not normal and we may need to assess that further. So if you're experiencing severe symptoms like that, do let us know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that's very helpful to know. That covers everything for me. I don't have any more questions. Thanks for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! Just to confirm — have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all of my questions have been answered. Thank you so much for your assistance!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care and best wishes with your recovery!
